data.hypothesis: The prior valid SIMD candidate retained an explicit AVX2 dispatch for widths at least 8; all measured correctness widths were at least 32, so its scalar-loop SIMD directives did not isolate compiler-generated SIMD on the tested hot path. This candidate removes that dispatch while preserving the scalar per-pixel noise and turbulence formulas, and uses OpenMP SIMD clones across adjacent pixels. Dependent permutation lookups may limit vectorization or make it slower; only full-call measurements can decide.

memory_lessons.applicability: SIMD directive experiments should ensure the measured sizes execute the directive-controlled path rather than an earlier width-based intrinsic dispatch.
memory_lessons.claim: The source snapshot dispatches widths at least 8 to the explicit AVX2 path, while the prior correctness cases used widths 32 through 768. That prior valid result was slightly slower than baseline, but does not establish the performance of a compiler-vectorized scalar path.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this candidate across the specified sizes and inspect compiler vectorization diagnostics if available; preserve the measured full-call result even if the implementation is slower.

data.notes: One source-only variant: removes the intrinsic AVX2 kernel and keeps scalar per-lane formulas, with compiler SIMD clones and a SIMD directive over each row. The fixed target is supplied as AMD EPYC 9654 with GCC 14.2, but exact build flags are unknown. No speedup or correctness result is claimed; the controller should validate all cases, including tails, and measure full-call time.
transformations: Removed the AVX2 intrinsic implementation and width-based dispatch so the measured loop evaluates the compiler-vectorized scalar formulation.
Preserved scalar gradient selection, permutation lookups, interpolation ordering, and turbulence accumulation per lane.

Added OpenMP declare simd clones to relevant scalar helpers, with row-invariant arguments marked uniform where applicable, and an OpenMP SIMD directive over adjacent output pixels so compiler tail handling remains general.
